Header: Orseolia oryzae Gol masi or Noli masi

Prevention: Avoid excessive use of nitrogenous fertilizer
BRRI Dhan33, a resistant rice variety in transplant
Consider growing other crops alongside rice as these may provide natural enemies for gall midge contol
Conserve paspalum grass in the field as it may harbour natural enemies of the midge
Remove wild rice as it is a secondary host for midges
Monitoring: Use light traps to monitor pest incidence
Freshly hatched larvae move into the growing point of the plant and feed inside
Feeding stimulates leaf sheath to transform into galls, known as 'onion shoot' or 'silver shoot' at tillering stage
Tillers with galls do not produce panicles
Check for adult gall midges at lights along roadside and at home
Direct Control: Use light traps with a bowl of soapy water under each trap
Hang yellow sticky traps above the crop to attract (and kill) adult gall midges
Restrictions: Don't apply insecticide until 35 days after transplanting
Always use personal protective equipment when using chemical pesticides
